newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits little changed in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits little changed in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were little changed in moderate trade on Wednesday, with most traders sidelined ahead of the outcome of U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins speech to a Senate Banking panel at around 1400 GMT today, dealers said.
On Tuesday, Alan Greenspan told a House Banking committee the central bank would raise interest rates if needed to head off inflation, but suggested that might not happen anytime soon.
"Rates were steady to easier in the morning on some position adjustments," a local dealer said.
"The market is waiting to see what Alan Greenspan will say at his semi-annual congressional testimony to the Senate Banking committee later tonight," a local dealer said.

In day-to-day rates, Wednesday/Thursday eased 1/16 percentage point to 5-1/2 5-3/8 percent. Thursday/Friday was unchanged from Tuesday's 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent and week-fixed unchanged at 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent.

Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged at 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent and three-months unchanged at 5-3/4 5-5/8 percent. Nine- months eased 1/16 point to 5-7/8 5-3/4 percent and twelve-months eased 1/16 point to 6 5-7/8 percent. - P. Theseira (65-870-3085)
